12.0.0.en: It is mentioned in (Mt 16:6-12) that Christ directed His previous words to the scribes and Pharisees; now He turns to His disciples. This warning that follows is for them especially and for believers in general, and it is to guard against the sin of hypocrisy. Its clear example is the Pharisees, who represent the religious leadership of the Jews. They cared about the appearance of holiness, but inside they were full of evil, as is proved by their refusal to believe in Christ and even their attempt to catch Him in some error, because their pride refused to let the crowds leave them and follow Christ. He likened hypocrisy to leaven, because leaven gives a small piece of dough a large size, but the inside is only air bubbles. Leaven also works inside, away from the eyes, just as evil spreads inside the heart while the person shows an outward appearance of great holiness that is completely different from what is within him.

12.1.0.en: It is also mentioned in (Mt 10:26) that everything a person does of evil in this life will be made known on the day of judgment, in addition to the exposure of many of his sins as time passes during his life. Therefore there is no need for hypocrisy, which will be exposed and will reveal the shame of its owner.

12.2.0.en: It is mentioned in (Mt 10:27) that what the Pharisees do in secret will be exposed before the light of Christ, who knows what is in their hearts, and by the Gospel, which reveals the ugliness of the sin of hypocrisy.

12.2.1.en: "The housetops" means the loftiness of the proclamation of the Holy Spirit on the lips of the Apostles and preachers, who will expose sins, including hypocrisy.

12.2.2.en: It also means that the teachings of the disciples, which are spoken in secret to small numbers because of persecution, will gradually spread, and the time of peace will come when they will be proclaimed openly in the light and from high places such as the housetops, and many will hear them and believe.

12.2.3.en: Know that every evil you hide in your heart will be judged, so repent of it quickly, and keep away from the judging of others that you speak in secret. For everything will be exposed, and the one you judge may learn what you said about him in secret, and your relationship with him will worsen. Instead of evil talk, take care to speak about love and goodness, even with one person, and this love will gradually spread and be made known to all, and they will see it in your life and in the lives of those to whom you spoke of it.

12.3.s.en: (2) Not fearing, and witnessing to Christ

12.3.0.en: My beloved, this is the first time that Christ uses this expression toward His followers. He declares that they are His own beloved ones, whom He distinguishes from the rest of the evil world and keeps safe from it.

12.3.1.en: Christ deals with the problem of fear, despising all the violence and persecution that men inflict on His children, since the limit of their persecution is harm to the body, but they cannot harm the spirit; on the contrary, the spirit clings to God and grows in knowing Him. But the One worthy of being feared is God, who has authority over the spirit and the body. If the soul fears Him, it is saved from eternal torment and no longer fears people, because God keeps it from dangers, and no trial befalls it except by His permission.

12.4.0.en: Two sparrows were sold for a farthing, which was the lowest coin in use, and if a person bought four sparrows for two farthings, a fifth sparrow was given to him as a gift, so that the five sparrows cost two farthings. This sparrow that is without price, that is, the gift, is not forgotten by God; rather, He cares for it and gives it its food.

12.4.1.en: The five sparrows point to the five senses. They look for their food on the earth and fall into the fowler's net, but when they rise to heaven they eat the fruit of the trees. That is, if the senses descend to earthly things the devil hunts them, and if they ascend to heaven they gain spiritual fruits.

12.5.0.en: Christ confirms His care for us, however weak we may be, or despised and worthless in the eyes of people like this sparrow. He even cares for the finest details of our lives: "the very hairs of your head are all numbered," that is, He knows their number and knows the details of every hair in them. Therefore there is no room for fear or anxiety, as long as our God loves us and cares for us to this degree.

12.6.0.en: Christ shows the importance of declaring faith, and not merely being convinced of it in the heart, and its reward is enjoying eternity, because whoever bears witness to Christ on earth, Christ bears witness to him in heaven and gives him a place in eternity. The opposite is also true: whoever denies Him on earth, Christ also denies him in heaven, that is, rejects him, and he goes to eternal torment.

12.6.1.en: Confessing Christ is not only by declaring that you are a Christian, but by showing the truth, supporting the oppressed, and Christian conduct in holding fast to God's commandments and enduring suffering for their sake.

12.7.0.en: Blaspheme against the Holy Spirit. If a person denies Christ he can repent and be forgiven; but whoever blasphemes against the Holy Spirit, that is, rejects His work in him, which calls him to repentance, and remains persistent in sin all his life, will not be forgiven. For one who denies Christ may afterward respond to the work of the Holy Spirit in him, repent and regain his faith, but whoever refuses repentance has no salvation. Here appears the importance of the sacrament of repentance and confession, which is the only way to salvation.

12.8.0.en: Christ calls us not to fear the one who persecutes us, however violent he may be or however weak we may be, because the Holy Spirit works in us and teaches us what to say in these confrontations, as happened in the trials of the martyrs, and how they silenced the governors who tried them, however weak their education, intelligence or personalities. Do not be troubled by any confrontation in your life, but take refuge in prayer, confident of the power of God that is in you.

12.9.s.en: (3) The parable of the rich fool

12.9.0.en: Disputes over inheritance often arise between brothers, and it was customary to ask the teachers to settle such cases. It seems that one of them was greedy and wanted to take a greater share of the inheritance than he deserved.

12.10.0.en: Christ refused to be a judge and a divider of the inheritance, because His aim is spiritual, namely the salvation of the soul, and not an earthly kingdom. By this they were also trying to catch Him in an error, namely that He had set Himself up as a civil judge without permission from the civil or religious authority.

12.11.0.en: "His life," that is, his happiness on earth, is a gift from God to His children.

12.11.1.en: Then Christ confronted the real problem in the strife among people, which is greed for material things, and He declared a clear truth: a happy life is not by money but by being with God. So why the love of money?

12.12.0.en: Christ told them a parable: a rich man had many fields, and in one year the produce of his land was greater than in all the past years, and so his barns could not hold it. He did not think of distributing this good to the needy, but was preoccupied with how to find many barns to hold all this good, to use it for himself alone.

12.13.0.en: "My fruits and my goods": he attributed the good to himself and did not thank God.

12.13.1.en: "Laid up for many years": this rich man forgot that he does not know when his life will end, and he supposed that he had many years ahead, so he did not prepare for his eternity by doing good.

12.13.2.en: "Eat, drink, and be merry": he thought that joy is in much eating and drinking and not in God, as if he were an animal concerned only with food, and not a human being with a spirit that is satisfied and rejoices in God.

12.13.3.en: This rich man thought of solving his problem by pulling down his barns and building greater ones to hold the fruit of his abundant crops. He felt reassured and glad, and told his soul to enjoy itself, since it had security in the abundance stored with him, enough fruit for the many years to come in his life.

12.14.0.en: "Thy soul shall be required of thee": you will die and your spirit will be separated and stand before the just Judge to be held to account for its preoccupation with material things instead of God.

12.14.1.en: "Whose shall those things be?": you will have no authority over all these goods you have acquired; rather they will be distributed to others, that is, those who inherit from you, and some of them may be people you do not want to give to. You will take nothing of them, and they will be given to others.

12.14.2.en: "Layeth up treasure for himself": he is selfish, gathering the goods of the earth for himself and not to give in charity to the needy, although he is rich and has much in excess.

12.14.3.en: "Not rich toward God": he did not care about loving God and worshipping Him, nor did he care about doing good to the needy, so as to lay up a treasure for himself in heaven.

12.14.4.en: On the day when the rich man thought these thoughts, God spoke to him, warning him that he would die that night and would not benefit from all these material goods.

12.14.5.en: So everyone who relies on material things without God is a fool and ignorant, who does not know how to live, because life is in God, who remains with him forever.

12.14.6.en: Ask yourself at the end of every day: how much was I occupied with the love of money, and how much time was I occupied with the love of God?

12.15.0.en: "Therefore": because of this, which He showed in the parable of the rich fool, the vanity of material things.

12.15.1.en: Christ confronts the problem of all people, which is attachment and preoccupation with material things, and calls them not to be concerned about food and clothing, directing their gaze to the purpose of all these means, which is the life that we should enjoy with God.

12.15.2.en: How strange it truly is that a person is occupied with the means rather than the goal, and so loses the goal. At the beginning of every day, remember your goal, which is the love of God, and leave aside the cares of the world and useless arguments.

12.16.0.en: Christ gives a clear example of not being concerned about food, namely the birds, of which He chose the ravens. Although they are unloved birds, and do not trouble themselves to provide their food, for they do not sow, nor reap, nor gather, nor care about preparing dwellings in which to live, yet God feeds them from the leftovers of the crops scattered in the world. If God cares for the birds, how much more for man, the head of all creation?

12.17.0.en: "That which is least": an increase in the height of one of you of about 50 cm is a small thing compared with the whole creation of man, which God made.

12.17.1.en: "The rest": the needs of man for food and clothing.

12.17.2.en: Then He gives a logical proof that we should not be anxious about food: however much a person is concerned, he cannot add one cubit to his stature (that is, about half a meter). If he cannot increase his height, he likewise cannot preserve his body; rather it is God who preserves it for him and provides for his material needs.

12.17.3.en: So man is unable to do the least thing, and therefore he must depend on God who created him and provides all his needs.

12.18.0.en: "They toil not, they spin not": she takes care to make her appearance and her clothing.

12.18.1.en: "O ye of little faith": a call to us to believe in God's fatherhood and in His provision for our lives, so that we are not anxious and occupied with our material needs. Christ gives us an example of not being concerned about clothing, namely the flowers with their beautiful colors and forms, which man tries to imitate, making his clothes like their colors and forms; but the original, the natural flowers, are better in appearance, for Solomon the king in all his glory, with his splendid clothing, did not reach the beauty of these flowers, that is, the lilies. These lilies are grasses, that is, plants that grow in the field for a few months, then dry up and are cast into the oven (the furnace). If God cares for them and gives them this beautiful form, will He not care about our clothing and our appearance if we believe in Him and rely on Him?

12.19.0.en: "Your Father": He declares God as a Father who cares for His children and knows all their needs.

12.19.1.en: "Shall be added": because God gives us life with Him, which is the most important, and then adds to it the needs of the body.

12.19.2.en: Here He gives the conclusion, which is not to be anxious about food and clothing, for the whole world runs after them; but we, the children of God, trust in our God who provides our needs, so that we seek what is more important, namely the reign of God over our hearts, and all material needs are a small thing that He calls the rest, and it is guaranteed from the hand of God who cares for us. Remember God's care for you and for all the creation around you, so that you do not worry about anything.

12.20.0.en: Christ calls His children who believe in Him the little flock, because the believers who walk according to His commandments are a minority, not only at the time of His presence on earth but even until now, since man is easily drawn to evil. But He reassures them that He is their Father and that they are distinguished from the whole world, because God has prepared the Kingdom for them and is glad to make them dwell in it.

12.20.1.en: Contemplate God's fatherhood: He is glad to give you the Kingdom, so that your heart may be at peace amid the afflictions of life, and this urges you to hold to His commandments in continual striving, so that you enjoy all that He has prepared for you.

12.21.0.en: "Sell": free yourselves from attachment to material things .... that is, sell them from your hearts.

12.21.1.en: "That ye have": all the material things you possess.

12.21.2.en: "Bags which wax not old": He likens the heavenly treasure to a bag that never perishes, in which are placed not silver and gold but works of mercy.

12.21.3.en: "A treasure in the heavens that faileth not": the nature of the world's wealth is that it is subject to decrease and ending, but the heavenly treasure remains forever.

12.21.4.en: Christ directs the attention of His children to how to prepare for the Kingdom, namely by giving alms to everyone in need, so that a person gives up all he has of money, health and various abilities and gives them in love to others. In this he transforms his material treasures, which are subject to theft and to corruption by time or insects, and sends these treasures to heaven by the work of mercy.

12.21.5.en: And by the work of mercy the treasure becomes one in heaven, so the heart is more attached to heaven, and increases in prayers and in doing good.

12.22.0.en: Christ also calls us to "let your loins be girded." The girdle is a leather belt tied around a person's waist so that he is ready for work. This belt is made from the skins of dead animals, so it signifies the death of the body to material attachments through fasting, detachment and the control of desires.

12.22.1.en: The preparation is completed by "lights burning." The lamp is the light that is in man, that is, the soul when it is enlightened by the love of God, spiritual worship and the acquiring of virtues.

12.23.0.en: "He shall gird himself": the master is Christ, who put on our body and girded Himself with it in order to bear in it all our sins and toils and to redeem us on the cross.

12.23.1.en: "Make them to sit down to meat": Christ gave rest to His children in His preaching on earth by healing the sick, casting out demons and feeding the crowds. All this is a symbol of the rest He gives them in the Kingdom, and of the great honor of their sitting in heavenly glory, and Christ serves them with His redeeming blood.

12.23.2.en: "Will come forth and serve them": when He was lifted up on the cross and shed His blood as a ransom for humanity. And He continues to serve them in the Kingdom with His blessings that never end.

12.23.3.en: Christ calls us to a fourth matter in preparing for the Kingdom, which is spiritual watchfulness, through the parable of a group of servants waiting for their master to return from the wedding, and He pronounces them blessed if they are watching.

12.23.4.en: These servants signify man's abilities and gifts, which await Christ who comes at His second coming from heaven, where His wedding with His angels is in joy and perpetual rejoicing. If the servants are always watching, they hasten to meet their master as soon as he knocks at the door, that is, calls them to end their life on earth and be with Him in heaven. Spiritual watchfulness is a person's attachment to spiritual worship and repentance and keeping away from the sources of sin, that is, constant concern for the salvation of the soul.

12.23.5.en: The master shows a love beyond the grasp of the mind, for he girds himself with a belt and comes forth and serves his servants himself. This signifies the love of Christ the Redeemer, who honors His believing children in the Kingdom and makes them glad by the merits of His blood shed on the cross, which He gave for their sake, and He glorifies them with Him forever.

12.24.0.en: Christ explains the importance of watchfulness in the previous parable: if the master comes in the second watch or the third watch of the night, that is, the second or third quarter of it, and finds them watching, he pronounces them blessed.

12.24.1.en: The first watch signifies childhood, the second manhood, and the third old age. So at whatever time God requires a person's soul, He finds him ready. He did not mention the first watch, because the child is lacking in understanding and in bearing responsibility for sin, so only the man or the old man is held to account. Also, it was not customary for anyone to return from a wedding in the first watch, which is from the beginning of the night at six in the evening until nine at night.

12.24.2.en: The second watch is from nine at night to twelve, that is, midnight, and the third watch from twelve to three in the morning. In ancient times it was also not customary to return in the fourth watch, which reaches six in the morning, that is, dawn.

12.25.0.en: This parable is mentioned in (Mt 24:42-44). "Broken through" means to dig and break into the walls of the house so that the thief enters through this breach and steals what he wants. He confirms the importance of watchfulness by another parable, which is guarding the house against thieves: since the master of the house does not know in what hour the thief will come, he must always watch so that his house is not broken into.

12.25.1.en: From all that has gone before, we must keep spiritual watchfulness, lest God require our lives at any time, or come at His second coming. Spiritual alertness means continual repentance, keeping away from the sources of sin, and attention to good works and service.

12.26.0.en: After Peter heard Christ's words about preparing for the Kingdom, he asked what was meant by the servants: were they Christ's disciples or all the crowds?

12.27.0.en: This parable is mentioned in (Mt 24:45-51). Christ answered Peter's question with another question, which He Himself will answer, namely who is the faithful and wise steward whom his lord sets over his servants.

12.27.1.en: The servants or attendants are the senses and abilities of man, and he is a steward over them to care for them and use them well. The servants also signify children, and parents are stewards from God to care for them and attend to their needs. Likewise the servants of the Church are responsible for caring for those they serve, whether children or adults.

12.27.2.en: So Christ's answer to Peter's question is that preparation for the Kingdom is directed to all the people and not only the Apostles; every person has responsibilities, is a steward over them, and must render an account of his stewardship to God.

12.28.0.en: Christ pronounces the faithful steward blessed, because he understood that his authority is taken from God and that he is only a steward, and so he was faithful in the details of his life. The reward of this steward is that the master sets him over all his goods, that is, gives him the eternal kingdom.

12.29.0.en: "My lord delayeth his coming": he neglects preparing for the Kingdom, forgetting that God may require him at any moment and end his life.

12.29.1.en: "To beat the menservants and maidens": he is harsh toward those he serves, so he has no sympathy for the needy or for sinners, and by his harshness he drives them away from the Kingdom.

12.29.2.en: "To eat and drink, and to be drunken": not only eating and drinking what his body needs, but being absorbed in drinking until drunkenness, that is, being immersed in material concerns.

12.29.3.en: "In a day when he looketh not for him, and at an hour when he is not aware": death comes suddenly to a person, at a time that the one who is not prepared for the Kingdom does not expect.

12.29.4.en: "Will cut him in sunder": will end his life.

12.29.5.en: "His portion": the reward of his life.

12.29.6.en: "The unbelievers": every unfaithful steward is unfaithful to his lord, and by them He means the wicked whom He casts into eternal torment, and by the unfaithful He also means the demons who disobeyed God.

12.29.7.en: But if the steward is unfaithful in caring for those he is responsible for, whether his senses or his children or those he serves in the Church, because of his absorption in his desires, this servant can expect nothing but his master's sudden coming to him to end his life and cast him with the wicked unfaithful into eternal torment.

12.29.8.en: It is understood from the above how important spiritual watchfulness is, by faithfulness in all the abilities that God has given us.

12.30.0.en: Christ makes clear that there are degrees in punishment and eternal torment. Whoever enjoyed the grace of the New Covenant and knew the love of Christ the Redeemer, and then violated His commandments, will be punished in eternity more than the one who committed the same errors but did not know Christ.

12.30.1.en: Whoever knows more about God and persists in sin, his punishment is severe; but whoever knows little about God or does not know God's commandments, his conscience is God's voice to him, and he is punished, but less than the former. If you have come to know the way of Christ and the Church, enjoy it, lest, if you neglect it, your punishment be fearful.

12.31.0.en: "Fire": the flame of the knowledge of the Holy Spirit in His children, which at the same time reveals the evil of the wicked, so they rise up against His children and persecute them; fire also signifies persecutions.

12.31.1.en: "Kindled": ignited, and this means the increase of the work of the Holy Spirit, who draws the hearts of many who sacrifice everything for His sake, since He was the first to bear these fires in His body by His death on the cross for the redemption of His children, so that they may learn from Him and take up their cross behind Him.

12.32.0.en: "Baptism" is the baptism of suffering that Christ accepted from His incarnation until the cross, so that all His believing children may walk the same way, enduring suffering for the sake of keeping His commandments and seeking all with love, bearing many toils like their Redeemer, until their love for Him is perfected and they depart to the paradise of bliss. "How am I straitened" means, I cannot but accomplish the redemption.

12.33.0.en: These words are also mentioned in (Mt 10:34-36).

12.33.1.en: At the level of the family, when some of its members believe, the other members rise against him, and the believer endures because his love for God is greater than his love for people however close they are to him. So a division occurs within the family between believers and unbelievers, caused by the evil of the unbelievers, and there is no peace in the relationships within the family, but the believers keep their inner peace in Christ Jesus.

12.34.0.en: The two are the Jews and the Gentiles, against three, that is, the Christians who believe in the Holy Trinity. The father signifies Satan, who sets himself up as father of the world against his pagan son who became a Christian. The mother is the synagogue of the Jews against her daughter, that is, the Church made up of Jews who became Christians. The mother-in-law also signifies the synagogue of the Jews, against her daughter-in-law, that is, the Gentiles who became Christians. Christ gives the example of a family made up of five persons, so that it divides two against three, and in detail the father rises against his son, the mother against her daughter, and the mother-in-law against her daughter-in-law (the wife of her son), and the reverse is also true. Do you hold to God's commandments even if the members of your household oppose you? And do you endure suffering with joy for the sake of Christ?

12.35.0.en: The world depended on agriculture as its basic craft, and the farmer was accustomed to discerning the natural phenomena that affect his farming, such as the mist that rains upon the plants so that they grow, and the south winds that carry warmth that helps growth.

12.35.1.en: Spiritually, the rains signify heavenly graces, and the hot south wind signifies the work of the Holy Spirit. This is what was accomplished by the Incarnation of Christ and His redemption, as He poured out salvation upon humanity and gave them the Holy Spirit who renews their nature.

12.36.0.en: If man understands how to discern the condition of the weather and what it foretells, why did the Jews not understand the prophecies of the prophets about Christ, whom they saw before them? Of course there are reasons, namely man's pride and his immersion in material things, which makes him lose the spirit of discernment and wisdom.

12.37.0.en: As an extension of the lack of discernment, a person does not call himself to account for his sins so as to repent and return to God, that is, he refuses to submit to the divine truth and goes further into sin, justifying himself.

12.38.0.en: It also appeared in the Sermon on the Mount (Mt 5:25). He gives a practical example, namely a dispute with an adversary: if you do not reconcile with him, you will stand before the judge who will pass judgment on your fault and deliver you to the officer, who will cast you into prison, and you will not come out of it until justice has received its full due. If you had seized something, you will serve days in prison for it, down to the last farthing (the smallest coin).

12.38.1.en: Besides calling us to settle disputes with others and to keep away from the courts with all our strength, it signifies spiritually the dispute with God. The adversary is the commandment, or the conscience, or the Holy Spirit; the judge is God the Judge on the last day; and the officer, as the Gospel of Matthew puts it, is the angels who cast the soul into prison, that is, eternal torment. Since our sins are unlimited, because they are directed against the unlimited God, we will not be able to pay the last farthing, but will remain in torment forever.

12.38.2.en: Submit to God's commandments, to the voice of your conscience and to the work of the Holy Spirit; obey your father of confession and the teachings of the Church, and hold fast to a life of repentance, and you will be saved on the last day and enjoy the heavenly Kingdom.

12.38.3.en: A call to repentance and spiritual striving. A call to repentance (vv. 1-5):

12.38.4.en: 1- There were present at that season some that told him of the Galilaeans, whose blood Pilate had mingled with their sacrifices. 2- And Jesus answering said unto them, "Suppose ye that these Galilaeans were sinners above all the Galilaeans, because they suffered such things? 3- I tell you, Nay: but, except ye repent, ye shall all likewise perish.

12.38.5.en: 4- Or those eighteen, upon whom the tower in Siloam fell, and slew them, think ye that they were sinners above all men that dwelt in Jerusalem? 5- I tell you, Nay: but, except ye repent, ye shall all likewise perish."
